target.title: fix(telegram): break long HTML chunks on word boundaries, not mid-word
target.body:
## Problem

`splitTelegramHtmlChunks()` in `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` hard-splits
long HTML text at the size limit. Its split-point helper
`findTelegramHtmlSafeSplitIndex` only avoids cutting HTML entities and UTF-16
surrogate pairs — it has no word/whitespace awareness, so any text run longer
than the chunk limit is sliced mid-word.

This is the layer-2 re-chunk mechanism reported in #104377 ("re-chunks
post-render by HTML length, cutting mid-word"): a long message rendered to HTML
and chunked here can split a word across two Telegram messages.

Extracted-logic repro on Node v22, input `"abcde abcde … "` at limit 13:

```
before: ["abcde abcde a","bcde abcde ab", …]   <- mid-word
after:  ["abcde abcde ","abcde abcde ", …]     <- word-safe
```

## Fix

Add `findTelegramHtmlWordSafeSplitIndex`, which prefers the last newline (then
the last other whitespace) inside the already entity-safe window.
`findTelegramHtmlSafeSplitIndex` uses that boundary when one exists and falls
back to the existing entity/surrogate-safe hard cut only when the window has no
interior whitespace, so a single token longer than the limit still hard-cuts.

Whitespace never occurs inside an HTML entity, so entity safety is preserved,
and every byte is preserved (chunks still join back to the original text).

## Tests

Added two cases to `format.test.ts`:
- long text breaks on word boundaries (never mid-word), content preserved;
- a single word longer than the limit still hard-cuts.

Existing `splitTelegramHtmlChunks` tests assert only per-chunk length bounds,
tag balance, entity/surrogate safety, and content preservation — all still hold.

## Verification

Split logic extracted and executed on Node v22: mid-word before, word-safe
after, entities intact, content preserved. The full repo test suite was not run
in this environment (no local checkout available); the change is scoped to one
helper and is behavior-preserving except for the mid-word case.

target.title: fix(channels): fix five channel lifecycle/shutdown bugs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Five small channel reliability bugs where lifecycle/shutdown paths can leak timers, unhandled rejections, or ignore abort signals.

1. **iMessage RPC client** `stop()` left a 500ms SIGTERM fallback timer running when the child process had already exited, keeping the event loop alive unnecessarily.
2. **Telegram webhook** shutdown could produce an unhandled promise rejection if `bot.stop()` or transport close threw inside the abort listener.
3. **Telegram ingress worker** `stop()` was not idempotent and could leak a second 15s terminate timer; `worker.terminate()` rejections were unhandled.
4. **Telegram probe** transport cache eviction closed the oldest transport with `void transport.close()`, so a rejecting `close()` became an unhandled rejection.
5. **ClickClack gateway** reconnect backoff used a raw `setTimeout` that ignored `abortSignal`, so stopping the gateway could wait the full reconnect delay. It also leaked an abort listener on every normal reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made
- iMessage: store the fallback timer, `unref` it, and clear it once the child-close race settles.
- Telegram webhook: catch shutdown errors inside the abort paths, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned transport/status cleanup even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- Telegram ingress worker: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.
- Telegram probe: wrap the close result with `Promise.resolve(...).catch(...)` so both sync and async rejections are swallowed safely.
- ClickClack gateway: reconnect backoff uses the shared `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, treating abort rejection as normal gateway termination instead of a local timer/listener.
- Telegram probe test: use `vi.stubEnv` for `NODE_ENV`/`VITEST` so Vitest teardown restores them, instead of direct `process.env` assignment that leaked production-mode values to worker siblings.

This update also fixes the `check-test-types` failures reported by ClawSweeper (iMessage child mock typing and ClickClack config narrowing) and strengthens the iMessage test to assert the timer is cleared immediately on settlement, not only after it would have fired.

## User Impact
Cleaner shutdown for channel gateways and fewer uncaught/unhandled rejection crashes during abort, restart, or transport eviction.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2.

The proof now includes a standalone real-gateway run for the ClickClack reconnect backoff fix (local HTTP + WebSocket servers driving the real `startClickClackGatewayAccount` production function), plus the regression-test negative controls used earlier.

### ClickClack gateway: real reconnect run with local servers

This script starts real local HTTP and WebSocket servers, configures `startClickClackGatewayAccount` to point at them, waits for the websocket cycle to start, forces a reconnect, then aborts. With the fix the gateway run resolves in ~50 ms instead of waiting the configured 60 s reconnect delay.

```bash
node --import tsx proof-clickclack-reconnect.mts
```

```typescript
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import type { ChannelGatewayContext } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-contract";
import { startClickClackGatewayAccount } from "./extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.js";
import type { ResolvedClickClackAccount } from "./extensions/clickclack/src/types.js";

function assert(description: string, condition: boolean) {
  if (condition) console.log(`  ok: ${description}`);
  else { console.log(`  FAIL: ${description}`); process.exitCode = 1; }
}

async function startClickClackMockServers() {
  const connections: WebSocket[] = [];
  const httpServer = createServer((req, res) => {
    const url = new URL(req.url ?? "/", `http://localhost`);
    res.setHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");
    if (url.pathname === "/api/me") {
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ user: { id: "bot-1", display_name: "Bot", handle: "bot", avatar_url: "", created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }));
    } else if (url.pathname === "/api/realtime/events") {
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ events: [] }));
    } else {
      res.statusCode = 404;
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: "not found" }));
    }
  });
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: httpServer });
  wss.on("connection", (ws) => { connections.push(ws); });
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => httpServer.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const addr = httpServer.address() as AddressInfo;
  return { httpUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${addr.port}`, httpServer, wss, connections };
}

async function main() {
  const { httpUrl, httpServer, wss, connections } = await startClickClackMockServers();
  const abort = new AbortController();
  const ctx: ChannelGatewayContext<ResolvedClickClackAccount> = {
    cfg: { channels: { clickclack: { baseUrl: httpUrl, token: "test-token", workspace: "wsp_test", reconnectMs: 60_000 } } } as any,
    accountId: "default",
    account: {} as ResolvedClickClackAccount,
    runtime: {} as any,
    abortSignal: abort.signal,
    log: { warn: () => {}, info: () => {}, error: () => {}, debug: () => {} },
    getStatus: () => ({ accountId: "default" }) as any,
    setStatus: () => {},
  };

  const start = Date.now();
  const runPromise = startClickClackGatewayAccount(ctx);

  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    const check = setInterval(() => { if (connections.length > 0) { clearInterval(check); resolve(); } }, 10);
  });

  for (const ws of connections) ws.close();
  abort.abort();
  await runPromise;
  const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

  assert(`gateway run resolved in under 5s (actual ${elapsed}ms)`, elapsed < 5_000);

  httpServer.close();
  wss.close();
  console.log("\nPROOF ASSERTIONS: all passed");
}

main().catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });
```

Terminal output (fix):

```text
=== ClickClack reconnect backoff real behavior proof ===
Node: v22.22.0

[case 1] startClickClackGatewayAccount aborts promptly during reconnect backoff
  ok: gateway run resolved in under 5s (actual 50ms)
  ok: reconnectMs was 60s, so a raw setTimeout would have hung

[case 2] raw setTimeout reconnect wait ignores abort (negative control)
  ok: raw setTimeout wait did NOT resolve early (actual 5002ms >= 4500ms)
  ok: resolved flag is false because the 60s timer never fired

=== Summary ===
PROOF ASSERTIONS: all passed
```

The second case demonstrates the old raw-`setTimeout` behavior: aborting has no effect, so the wait continues for the full delay. The first case shows the fixed production gateway reacting to abort immediately while a real reconnect delay is pending.

### Regression-test negative controls

These temporarily restore the `origin/main` source for each fix, run the relevant test to reproduce the bug, then restore the fix and show the test passes.

#### ClickClack reconnect backoff ignores abort

Negative control (`extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
$ timeout 12 pnpm test extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts -- --run -t "exits immediately when aborted during reconnect backoff"
[test] test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts exited by signal SIGTERM
exit=124 (timeout/hang)
```

Fix restored:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts -- --run -t "exits immediately when aborted during reconnect backoff"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 6 skipped (7)
   Duration  4.57s
exit=0
```

#### iMessage SIGTERM fallback timer leak

Negative control (`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts -- --run -t "clears the SIGTERM fallback timer"
 FAIL  |extension-imessage| extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts > IMessageRpcClient.stop > clears the SIGTERM fallback timer
AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0
    expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBe(0)
exit=1
```

Fix restored:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts -- --run -t "clears the SIGTERM fallback timer"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
   Duration  912ms
exit=0
```

#### Telegram webhook unhandled rejection on shutdown

Negative control (`extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Rejection ⎯⎯⎯
Error: bot stop failed
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
exit=1
```

Fix restored:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
exit=0
```

### Repro scripts

- `/tmp/proof-clickclack-reconnect.mts` — real ClickClack gateway reconnect run against local servers.
- `/tmp/proof-channel-lifecycle.sh` — automates the negative-control / restore cycle for the regression tests above.

## Evidence

All fixes are accompanied by regression tests:

```text
extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts                     2 passed
extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts                   30 passed
extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts    2 passed
extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts                     14 passed
extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts                  7 passed
```

Run locally with:

```bash
pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts -- --run
```

Local validation also passes:

```text
$ pnpm format:check extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ pnpm lint:all -- extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.ts
(no errors)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
(no errors)
```

### iMessage RPC client: real stop() timer cleanup

Drives the real `IMessageRpcClient` against a real spawned child process (node with bogus args exits -> close event) with real timers, and quantifies how long the process stays alive AFTER `stop()` settles. A leaked 500ms fallback timer keeps the process alive; a cleared one lets it exit immediately.

```bash
node --import tsx proof-imessage-stop.mts
```

Terminal output (fix):

```text
[case 1] IMessageRpcClient.stop does not leak the 500ms fallback timer
  Node: v22.22.0
  stop settled in 43ms; process exit at 43ms (post-stop wait 0ms)
  ok: process exits promptly after stop (no leaked 500ms fallback timer) (post-stop wait 0ms)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 1 passed, 0 failed
```

Negative control (`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
[case 1] IMessageRpcClient.stop does not leak the 500ms fallback timer
  Node: v22.22.0
  stop settled in 41ms; process exit at 508ms (post-stop wait 467ms)
  FAIL: process exits promptly after stop (no leaked 500ms fallback timer) (post-stop wait 467ms)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 0 passed, 1 failed
```

The main version leaves the 500ms SIGTERM fallback timer ref'd and uncleared, so the process waits ~467ms for it to fire before exiting. The fix clears the timer in `finally`, so the process exits immediately (post-stop wait 0ms).

### Telegram shutdown paths: proof boundary

The Telegram webhook and ingress-worker shutdown fixes are covered by the regression-test negative controls below (real `startTelegramWebhook` with a mock bot whose `stop()` rejects; real `createTelegramIngressWorker` stop idempotency). A standalone real-setup proof for these paths requires a live Telegram bot token and a public webhook endpoint, which is not available in this contributor environment (per the local proof matrix, Telegram channel proofs need bot credentials + a public callback). The iMessage and ClickClack real-production proofs above cover the same fix shape (lifecycle/timer cleanup on shutdown); maintainer validation on a real Telegram setup is requested for the two Telegram shutdown paths.

---

@clawsweeper re-review

Patch-quality findings from the previous review are addressed:
- [P1] ClickClack reconnect backoff now reuses the shared `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (treating abort rejection as normal gateway termination) instead of a local timer/listener.
- [P3] Telegram probe test uses `vi.stubEnv` for `NODE_ENV`/`VITEST` so teardown restores them.

Real behavior proof added for the iMessage shutdown path: a standalone script drives the real `IMessageRpcClient` against a real spawned child with real timers, quantifying post-stop wait (0ms fix vs 467ms main negative control). This joins the existing ClickClack real-gateway proof.

Proof boundary: the Telegram webhook and ingress-worker shutdown paths rely on the regression-test negative controls in the body; a standalone real-setup proof needs a live bot token + public webhook (not available in this contributor environment). Requesting evaluation under Maintainer option 1 (accept the iMessage + ClickClack real proofs and the Telegram regression-test negative controls as the mergeable proof surface), or option 2 if a maintainer can validate the Telegram shutdown paths on a real setup.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix: enable no-floating-promises lint and separate UI tsconfig (#104386)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #104386. Two preventive tooling hardenings that close measured gaps in the type/lint surface:

1. **`no-floating-promises` not enabled**: The repo's async-heavy gateway codebase had no rule catching unawaited promises (swallowed errors, races). Only `no-misused-promises` was configured.

2. **Node-side code typechecks against browser globals**: `tsconfig.core.json` includes `src/`, `ui/`, and `packages/` in one program with `lib: ["DOM", "DOM.Iterable", "ES2023"]`, giving server code access to `window`/`document`/`navigator`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to #104348 (scripts tsgo lane) and #104313 (harness hardening). The fix follows the existing dedicated-lane architecture pattern.

## User Impact

No behavior change. Purely preventive hardening:
- Catches a new class of async bugs at lint time
- Removes misleading DOM types from Node-side code while preserving them for legitimate browser consumers (extensions/diffs, extensions/canvas)

## Evidence

**Before:**
```jsonc
// .oxlintrc.json - no-floating-promises missing
// tsconfig.core.json - lib: ["DOM", "DOM.Iterable", "ES2023"] includes ui/**
```

**After:**
```jsonc
// .oxlintrc.json
"typescript/no-floating-promises": "error"

// tsconfig.core.json - Node-only libs
"lib": ["ES2023", "ScriptHost"],
"include": ["src/**/*", "packages/**/*"],
"exclude": ["ui/**"]

// tsconfig.ui.json - DOM-enabled UI project
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["DOM", "DOM.Iterable", "ES2023"]
  },
  "include": ["ui/**/*"]
}
```

**Changes:**
- `.oxlintrc.json`: adds `no-floating-promises` rule and `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/Resources/CanvasA2UI/a2ui.bundle.js` to ignorePatterns
- `tsconfig.core.json`: removes DOM libs, excludes `ui/**`
- `tsconfig.ui.json`: new DOM-enabled project for `ui/**`
- `tsconfig.core.projects.json`: references `tsconfig.ui.json`
- `package.json`: adds `tsgo:ui` command, updates `tsgo:prod` to include it
- `scripts/check-changed.mjs`: routes core lane changes through `tsgo:ui`

The generated A2UI bundle (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/.../a2ui.bundle.js`) is now explicitly ignored alongside the other two a2ui bundles.

target.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
target.body:
Related: #51620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose inbound message was accepted shortly before a SIGUSR1 or config reload could have buffered message content silently dropped before it reached the reply pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now closes ordinary work admission synchronously, flushes accepted inbound debounce work inside one core-private restart continuation, drains channel, active-turn, and followup work in order, then rechecks work created by followup delivery. Pre-created debounce callbacks reserve tracked required-continuation ownership, including parentless accepted work. Already-reserved required continuations may finish during the signal-pending gap while ordinary roots remain fenced, and removed-but-unsettled timer flushes remain visible until settlement. Buffered callbacks can also be explicitly rebound to the private restart admission context, while the global sweep is bounded by both the remaining restart deadline and a 100-pass/30-second ceiling so continued ingress cannot stall reload indefinitely.

Every non-forced phase now shares one absolute restart-drain deadline. Initial active-task and embedded-run waits receive only the budget remaining after inbound debounce and channel queue draining, so earlier phases cannot reset the configured maximum.

Forced restarts retain the existing skip-drain behavior. This does not persist messages sent while the gateway is offline.

## User Impact

Messages accepted immediately before an in-process reload can complete through the normal command/reply path instead of being rejected by the restart fence or disappearing from in-memory buffers. A sustained stream of new transport events also cannot hold the gateway forever in the debounce-flush phase, and the configured restart deferral maximum is honored across the full drain sequence.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation for `bb8f1b842e85c6745e7f8a1bfb8303d73ca6f7f6`:

- **Focused behavior tests:** 4 files, 167 tests passed.
  - `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`: 65 passed.
  - `src/process/command-queue.test.ts`: 42 passed.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.
